column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly calls her “his concubine”; BSB uses “she.” It says she went away from him, without a separate verb meaning “return.”
The Hebrew says “speak to her heart,” retaining a bodily image behind BSB’s “speak kindly to her.” It calls her father “the girl’s father,” where BSB uses “her father.”
The Hebrew has separate finite verbs for their eating, drinking, and lodging; BSB makes these activities participles.
The Hebrew says that they rose early, then that he rose to go. BSB makes the preparation to depart plural.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew separately says that he returned and spent the night; BSB compresses this into “stayed there that night.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew ends with “you shall go to your tent”; BSB renders the tent as “home.”
The Hebrew repeats “with him” for the donkeys and the concubine; BSB combines them under one “with.”
The Hebrew has a separate “come, please” before “let us turn aside.” It says to lodge “in it,” referring to the city, rather than BSB’s “here.”
The Hebrew says “a foreign city” and that its inhabitants are not of the sons of Israel. BSB says “the city of foreigners” and “there are no Israelites.”
The Hebrew explicitly says that he spoke “to his servant.” It calls the destinations “places” and has no separate word corresponding to BSB’s “try.”
The Hebrew says Gibeah “which belongs to Benjamin”; BSB says “in Benjamin.”
The Hebrew leaves the subject of “he entered and sat” unnamed; BSB identifies him as “the Levite.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says he “lifted his eyes”; BSB renders the bodily expression as “looked up.”
The Hebrew leaves the speaker unnamed, where BSB supplies “the Levite.” It repeats Bethlehem in Judah instead of reducing the second mention to Bethlehem.

The Hebrew calls the woman “your maidservant” and describes the young man as “with your servants.” BSB says “the maidservant” and “young man with me,” then places “your servants” in the final statement.
The Hebrew says “all your need is upon me”; BSB turns the expression of responsibility into “Let me supply everything you need.”
Close to the Hebrew.

The Hebrew describes making their heart merry and calls the attackers “sons of worthlessness.” BSB renders these expressions as “enjoying themselves” and “wicked men.” The demand literally uses “know him.”
The Hebrew says the man “came into my house”; BSB explicitly calls him “a guest.”
The Hebrew explicitly says “humble them” and “what is good in your eyes”; BSB renders these as “use them” and “as you wish.”
The Hebrew calls the man “the man,” where BSB supplies “the Levite.” It uses “knew her” for the sexual act and says he “brought her out” rather than “sent her outside.”
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly calls her “the woman, his concubine”; BSB retains only “his concubine.”
The Hebrew says he went “to his place”; BSB renders this as “for home.”
The Hebrew describes the division in relation to her bones; BSB renders this as “limb by limb”.
The Hebrew first says that nothing like this “has happened,” then that it “has been seen.” BSB reverses the order and uses “done” for the first expression.
